key_facts: Ordinary build/publish is not forced to use AOT; AOT is opt-in for a Windows title while the page explains console JIT restrictions.
The AOT analyzers exclude netstandard2.0, and the project clears AOT-related global properties for that target.
Source-generated marshalling and unmanaged callbacks support the modern .NET AOT contract.
CI ILC compilation is not a packaged live sandbox/sign-in test; live validation remains manual.
acceptable_uncertainty: Answer from this pinned revision, not a claim to have published or exercised a title.
A feature classification is acceptable only when it explains that the requested behavior/documentation already exists.
avoid: Saying netstandard2.0 is AOT-published or AOT is mandatory for every Windows build.
Claiming CI proves live sign-in, console certification, or all runtime behavior.
Suggesting reflection/dynamic marshalling as an AOT workaround or a new API without need.
Requesting generic reproduction information for an answerable documentation question.
